newsitem.title: USA: Apple sees substantial Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Apple sees substantial Q2 loss.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Monday said it expects to report a "substantial" loss in the second quarter of fiscal 1997 due to the company's previously- announced purchase of NeXT Software Inc and restructuring charges.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Apple said the purchase of NeXT will now cost about $430 million, up from a previous estimate of $400 million. The company also said it does not expect to return to profability until "at least the fourth quarter of 1997, if not later."

Apple did not estimate how much the loss for the fiscal second quarter, ending March, will be. Most of the loss will come from the charge Apple will take to pay for the NeXt purchase, the company said.

Apple also said it expects its research and development costs to be relatively flat in the scond quarter compared with the same quarter a year ago. Its selling, general and administrative costs also will decrease slightly in the second quarter because of lower advertising and marketing expenditures, the company said.
Previously, Apple executives had said they expected the company to be profitable by the fourth quarter. They had also said they would pay $400 million in cash and stock for the NeXT acquisition.
